newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee quiet on overseas dlr lethargy.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee quiet on overseas dlr lethargy.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee was range-bound in early Monday trade due to a subdued U.S. dollar overseas and a lack of importer activity, dealers said.
At 0430 GMT, the rupee was at its opening level of 58.48 to the dollar.
"The dollar, which is moving sideways overseas, is keeping speculators away," said an ABN Amro Bank dealer. "There has been no import covering either so far to create some movement."
The Central Bank pushed down the dollar by one local cent, fixing buying and selling prices at 58.1848 and 59.3602.
Overnight call money rates were at 11.50 percent, after opening at 16 percent, due to big state bank lending, dealers said.
